title: Appearance surfaces for the lighting pass
description: The lighting pass decomposes an image's appearance into surfaces, in pass order, with one atomic question each. light_ledger instantiates the questions per emitter, subject and pair; answers are yes, no or unknown and are recorded as observations under terms[0]. This structure does not establish observer reliability or validate the selected surfaces.
basis: atomic question graphs for image evaluation (Davidsonian scene graph, Cho et al. 2024); marks drawn on the image so the model refers to ids (Set-of-Mark, Yang et al. 2023); light direction from occluding contours (Johnson and Farid 2005). These references motivate the methods, not this particular surface selection or its agreement cutoffs; those remain unverified implementation policy pending human review.
coordinates: image pixels, x right, y down; a vector [-0.7, -0.7] points to the upper-left
subjects: each is {id, bbox, depth?, mask?}. A box is the cheapest way to point at a thing and the most expensive to measure: whatever else sits in it is measured as if it were the subject, which is what keeps albedo, ambient and specular from separating a dark strap inside a shirt box, and what keeps the shaded mass from being read on a frame without alpha. mask is the path of an image whose alpha marks the subject, canvas-sized or box-sized: a layer export, which layered hand-drawn work already has and which no segmentation recovers, since a rock and the sand under one warm light share their chroma. The game still ships one flattened sprite; only the package carries the layers.

scopes.subject: one question per subject
scopes.pair: per subject, against the emitter it should answer to (highest irradiance proxy: luminance x area over squared distance, depth layers widening the distance) and the emitter its shading points at; asked only where the angle does not decide. Only diffuse is asked this way: the surfaces judged against one light per subject are one list each, since the verdict names that light
scopes.global: one question for the whole image

decided_by.measurement: a ledger field decides the answer outside the contested band; the observer is asked only inside it, and a subject the measurement cannot place is unknown, never yes
decided_by.evidence: the ledger measures around the question and the observer decides it, reading those fields
decided_by.observer: nothing is measured; the observer decides and unknown is the honest default

surfaces.label: Emissive sources
surfaces.description: Anything that reads as producing light: lamps, neon, glowing bands, sky, screens. The ledger proposes the brightest blobs of the image; bright paint under a strong light is the classic false positive, so every candidate is confirmed or rejected before any pair question is answered. Each candidate is measured against its own neighbourhood (spill: surfaces within two core radii against surfaces four to eight out, in luminance and in distance to its hue) and against the subjects (receivers: how many point their shading at it). A candidate confirmed as a light that neither lifts its surroundings nor is pointed at by anything is a decal, whatever genre the frame is drawn in, and lands on asset_cohesion. Spill is not read where both rings sit in the bottom few code values of the 8-bit range: there the codec's ringing around a bright blob outweighs any light, and an export written in the wrong colour space then reads spill around a decal that lights nothing.
surfaces.question: Is {emitter} a light source rather than a bright surface?

surfaces.label: Key light
surfaces.description: The one direction that dominates form shading across the subjects. When no confirmed emitter sits in that direction the key is off screen and only its direction is recorded.
surfaces.question: Does one light direction dominate the shading across the subjects?

surfaces.label: Diffuse form shading
surfaces.description: The lit side, terminator and form shadow of one subject against one emitter. The ledger measures where the bright side points and the angle to the emitter; the observer decides whether that emitter should be lighting the subject at all.
surfaces.question: Does the bright side of {subject} face {emitter}?

surfaces.label: Specular highlight
surfaces.description: The brightest accent on a subject: it sits on the side facing the light that subject answers to. The ledger's highlight is the subject's brightest region, which on a subject with a bright painted band is that band and not a specular; the brightest region also lies inside the bright side, so on a box without a material mask no measurement separates the two. One list, judged against the light the verdict names, and answered from looking. The colour half of an accent belongs to light_color, so that this question asks one thing.
surfaces.question: Does the highlight on {subject} sit on the side facing the light it answers to?

surfaces.label: Light colour cast
surfaces.description: The warm or cool cast of lit surfaces against the colour of the light that reaches them. A warm lamp that leaves every lit surface neutral or cool is the most common defect of generated images. One list, judged against the light the verdict names.
surfaces.question: Do the lit surfaces of {subject} take the colour of the light it answers to?

surfaces.label: Cast shadow
surfaces.description: Shadow thrown away from the light: onto other surfaces, and onto the subject's own parts, where a helmet darkens a face and a strap darkens a shirt. The ledger measures where a subject's shaded mass sits against its lit side, which must be opposite it. That needs no emitter at all, so a lone sprite can be judged on it, and it is the surface that catches shading painted for looks rather than for a light. It is read only where the subject's pixels are known -- a subject mask, or the file's own alpha: without either, the bottom decile of a box is the ground behind the subject, and any frame-wide gradient (a vignette, a sky, a floor falloff) turns that ground into a confident direction. It cannot separate a cast shadow from the form shadow inside one box, cannot see a missing contact shadow on the ground, and says nothing about a subject too flat to carry directional shading, so a subject the observer lists overrides it.
surfaces.question: Does the shadow of {subject} fall away from the light, onto its own parts and onto what it stands on?

surfaces.label: Ambient, bounce and occlusion
surfaces.description: What the unlit side looks like: filled by ambient or bounce, darkened where surfaces meet. Observation only: the fill of an unlit side is albedo-invariant per material, so it would be measurable on one material at a time, and a box holds as many as the artist drew. A subject mask is what would make it one.
surfaces.question: Is the unlit side of {subject} filled by ambient or bounce light and darkened where it meets other surfaces?

surfaces.label: Rim and backlight
surfaces.description: A bright edge on the side away from the key, implying a source behind the subject. Legitimate only when such a source exists in the frame or in the scene's light rig.
surfaces.question: Does a rim light on {subject} correspond to a source behind it?

surfaces.label: Atmosphere and depth
surfaces.description: Contrast and saturation falling with distance, haze between planes, glow around emitters. Observation only.
surfaces.question: Do farther subjects lose contrast and saturation relative to nearer ones?

surfaces.label: Albedo
surfaces.description: The base colour that remains once lighting is removed. One material reads as one albedo wherever it appears; a highlight or a colour cast is not a change of material.
surfaces.question: Does the material of {subject} read as one base colour wherever it appears in the image?

answers.style.mode: physical (lights in the frame) | fake_lighting (one stylistic key, lighting.fake_lighting) | engine_lit (sprites the engine lights: painted shading is a defect)
answers.emitters: proposed id -> lamp | neon | sky | screen | glow | paint | unknown. paint is a judgment and rejects the emitter, voiding every pair with it (a parent answered no counts its children as no, after Cho et al. 2024). unknown is a hold and not a judgment: the blob is not confirmed, so nothing is judged against it, but it keeps a row as unclassified and holds asset_cohesion at warn. A form handed back unfilled holds every proposed emitter this way, which is why an unanswered frame never reads pass
answers.image_sha256: the image the sheet was filled for, stamped by phase one. Emitter ids are ordinal by brightness, so they rebind when the pixels change: a re-export, a colour grade or a different crop can make e2 a different blob than the one answered about. Phase two refuses a sheet stamped for another image; a hand-written sheet may omit the field
answers.pairs[].answer: yes | no | unknown, only for the diffuse pairs the form lists: the band where the measurement does not decide. The form handed back unfilled is a valid answer sheet: it returns what the measurement decides and unknown elsewhere
answers.subjects.<surface>: null until the observer writes on that subject-scope surface, then {no: [subject ids], unknown: [subject ids]}: every subject the answered surface does not list answers yes and nothing is recorded for it. A surface left null is unanswered, not agreed, and returns unknown for every subject, so a form handed back as issued never reads yes anywhere. cast_shadow is the one exception and runs the other way: a subject nobody lists falls through to the measurement

thresholds: agreement within 20 degrees is decided by measurement, beyond 60 likewise; between, the observer is asked. The emitter a subject answers to is its expected key (lamp, sky and screen outrank neon and glow; then the irradiance proxy), or the emitter it points at when that one is at least a quarter as strong. Light colour is the observer's: a subject box that holds a painted band has a highlight in the band's hue, which no measurement can tell from a cast until subjects carry material masks; hue_delta_deg and hue_shift_from_body_deg are hints only. Estimator noise on synthetic discs stays under 4 degrees (bright side) and 8 degrees (contour fit); these synthetic estimator checks do not validate the agreement cutoffs for artwork. The existing twenty and sixty degree bands are unverified implementation policy, retained for compatibility and awaiting measured evidence or an explicit human decision. Previous prose claimed a typical hand-drawn alignment and a suspicion cutoff without a recorded basis; neither claim is evidence. The shaded mass of a subject is read against its lit side on the same twenty and sixty degree bands, and only where the subject's pixels are known (a mask or the file's alpha) and the bright side is stronger than a flat sprite measures. A vignette of a tenth, invisible to an eye and on by default in a URP project, measures 0.40 of shaded strength on a box over a ground it never touched; under alpha the same gradient only bends the mass, and a heavy one costs about twenty degrees, which leaves the band the measurement settles and hands the subject to the observer. Spill and receivers carry no threshold at all: a sign and a count decide whether a confirmed light is one the frame answers to, and an unmeasurable neighbourhood (a lone sprite, a source at the border) stays unknown. Team precedent replaces these numbers.

levels.asserted: a ledger field named for the surface decides the answer and the observer agrees with it; direction claims also survive the mirror check
levels.estimated: answered from looking, or the surface has no ledger field
levels.unknown: the mirror check disagrees, the subject or emitter cannot be identified, or the evidence region is missing

style_exemption.rule: when the asset group's context declares fake lighting (a fixed stylistic light, common in pixel art), a diffuse or specular disagreement with the emitters, and a confirmed light the frame does not answer to, are recorded under intentional_contrast, not direction_compliance or asset_cohesion

record: light_ledger builds the observation record from the verdict: term_id = terms[0] of the surface, region = the subject's bbox (the emitter's bbox for emissive, whole_image for global scopes), level asserted where the measurement decided and estimated where the observer did, notes name subject and emitter ids and carry no magnitude
